proposal.hypothesis: Correct two-target-per-thread configurations with blocks of 96, 128, and 160 measured 0.002554, 0.002585, and 0.002567 seconds; the 256-thread parent measured 0.002745 seconds, all slower than the 0.001844-second baseline. Testing 192 threads (six warps) with 384 targets per block keeps source-register reuse and targets per thread fixed while testing whether intermediate CTA granularity balances scheduling overhead and parallelism. No speedup is assumed; the controller should check correctness and measure all scored sizes.

retained: Set block=192 and items_per_block=384, preserving two targets per thread and zero shared-memory allocation.
Retain the existing unique target mapping: target0 = blockIdx.x * (2 * blockDim.x) + threadIdx.x and target1 = target0 + blockDim.x, with independent bounds checks and one write per valid target.
Continue loading each source once per interaction-loop iteration and reusing its values across both target accumulations in registers.
